description: The v3 research Phase 2 bounded-locality feasibility corpus. Declares the pilot, its predeclared rejection rules, the main experimental conditions, the three control arms, and the GO/MODIFY/ABANDON gates -- all before any main-stage result was inspected. See docs/V3_PHASE2_LOCALITY_FEASIBILITY.md.
ruleset_note: EXPERIMENTAL. Not Ruleset 3, not a stable identity, not an Agent API v2 declaration. Bounded locality changes addressing and nothing else: vulnerable core, core beacon, scheduling, termination, scoring and the entrant action budget are all inherited from bytefray-rules-2 unchanged.
research_question: Does a bounded-locality mechanic make two strategic axes viable at the same time -- specifically, can it hold Beta2 Sec 17 criterion 2 (search both wins meaningful matchups AND owns the core-capture mechanism) across a density range wider than the narrow Ruleset-v2 band, without any single archetype reaching 90% across dissimilar rosters?

phase1_inheritance.density_is_the_axis: Phase 1 Sec 6.1 established that arena size and action budget are one variable, indexed by S = (instr_per_tick x ticks) / arena_size. Phase 2 therefore varies density explicitly and holds a scale check at constant density rather than treating arena and budget as independent knobs.
phase1_inheritance.arena_range_kept_narrow: Phase 2H preferred approach. Arena is restricted to {1024, 4096, 16384} -- a 16x span. Phase 1 Sec 10.1 measured Weights.territory_bucket = 64 giving 16 / 64 / 256 buckets at those sizes and survival shares of 19.1% / 7.4% / 4.6% of claimer's score. Arena 256 and below (where the territory term collapses to identically zero) and 65536 (where survival is 1.3%) are both excluded, so the known scoring-resolution confound stays bounded and locality is the only thing that changes.
phase1_inheritance.default_is_the_anchor: Phase 1 Sec 18 item 2: arena 4096 / budget 8 / 400 ticks is at or adjacent to the optimum of the tested Ruleset-v2 parameter space. It is the density anchor here, not a tuning target.
phase1_inheritance.criterion_2_is_the_discriminator: Phase 1 Sec 18 item 3: criteria 1, 3 and 4 pass everywhere in Ruleset v2 and are not useful discriminators on their own. Criterion 2 has two independently failable halves and is the primary gate below.

rosters.note: negative control: no offense present by construction. The Sec 17 criterion 5 exclusion, declared rather than inferred -- the direct analogue of the Phase 0 corpus's claimer_coredefender_reactive.
search-free kingmaking mechanism check for lclaimer_ltracker_ldefender.
search-free kingmaking mechanism check for lclaimer_ltracker_lreactive.
expansion + probing search + the stationary control.
expansion + sweeping search + the stationary control.
both defense variants against sweeping search.

roster_note: Eleven three-entrant rosters, structurally mirroring the eleven the Phase 0 control corpus and Phase 1 grid both used, with local_camper occupying the seat hunter held there. All eleven are kept because Sec 17 criterion 1 is scored by enumerating which agent leads each tested roster; a sampled subset could not be scored against the rubric verbatim. local_camper is a control, NOT a second expansion archetype -- the same discipline Phase 0 Sec 10.3 applied to hunter.

pairs.note: criterion 2's counter-strategy matchup: does dedicated search defeat blind expansion?

pilot.purpose: Bound the reasonable reach region before the main conditions are executed. Deliberately cheap and discardable: results are NOT counted as evidence anywhere except where a condition was promoted into the main stage.

conditions.probe: attack_infeasible: R < CORE_SIZE, so one burst cannot cover a whole core
smallest reach at which a burst can still cover a core
an eighth of the arena reachable from one locus
reach_collapse: a quarter of the arena reachable from one locus
global-reach control: R = arena/2 makes every cell reachable from anywhere, so locality is present in name only
low density (S=0.195) in a large arena: no-contact / crawl check
anchor density (S=0.781) in a small arena: reach relative to arena size

rejection_rules.attack_infeasible: locality_reach < 8 (CORE_SIZE): a single reachable burst cannot cover a whole core, so offense is impossible by construction rather than by strategy.
rejection_rules.reach_collapse: locality_reach >= arena_size / 4: so much of the arena is reachable from one locus that bounded locality cannot be strategically distinct from global access. Such a condition may still be RETAINED as an explicitly labelled global-reach control (Phase 2L Control 2), but never as an experimental condition.
rejection_rules.no_contact: a roster containing a dedicated search agent produced zero core captures in any cell -- entrants coexisted without ever contesting a core.
rejection_rules.movement_dominated: mean share of entrant actions spent on MOVE >= 0.50 across the roster: agents spend most of their budget merely reaching one another.
rejection_rules.crawl: mean realized ticks equals the tick limit AND mean summed final occupancy < 20%: matches run out the clock without meaningful interaction.
rejection_rules.turtle_dominant: local_camper (the stationary control) wins >= 50% in a roster that contains a dedicated search agent.
rejection_rules.runtime_pathology: any forfeit, any reach miss, or any non-zero evaluation exit code.

pilot.promotion_rule: The main stage's reach R* is the smallest surviving reach at which the pilot shows BOTH (a) core captures occurring in a search-containing roster and (b) a MOVE action share strictly below 0.50, preferring a reach that is a power of two and no larger than arena_size/32 so that bounded locality is unambiguously distinct from global access. If no reach satisfies both, that is itself an ABANDON finding (A7) and no main stage is run.

main.purpose: The controlled comparison. Three arms at matched conditions: bounded locality (L), a global-reach control on the identical runtime and population (G), and the Ruleset-v2 historical control (V) read from the committed Phase 1 artifacts without re-execution.

conditions.rationale: one density step below the anchor; the Ruleset-v2 control FAILS criterion 2 here (Phase 1 Sec 12).
the density anchor -- the shipped Ruleset-v2 default, which Phase 1 found at or adjacent to the optimum of the tested v2 space.
one density step above the anchor; the Ruleset-v2 control FAILS criterion 2 here, in the opposite direction (Phase 1 Sec 12.1).
anchor density at a 4x smaller arena. With R* fixed in absolute cells, this is also the condition where reach is largest relative to the arena.
low density at a 4x larger arena; the Ruleset-v2 control FAILS criterion 2 here.
anchor density at a 4x larger arena -- the constant-density scale check Phase 1 Sec 7 showed is the least-perturbed axis under Ruleset v2.

Phase 2L Control 2. Identical runtime, identical population, identical conditions, but R = arena/2 so every cell is reachable from anywhere. This is what separates the effect of bounded locality from the effect of having written new agents.
the same control one density step down, so the L-versus-G comparison is not read off a single point.

ruleset_v2_control.note: Phase 2L Control 1. The Ruleset-v2 arm is NOT re-executed: Phase 1 already measured exactly these conditions with the frozen v2 population, and its artifacts are read as-is. Re-running them would produce identical numbers at real cost.
ruleset_v2_control.ruleset_v2_band_on_this_ladder: Criterion 2 holds at exactly ONE density value on this six-condition ladder: S = 0.781. Every S = 0.195 condition and the S = 3.125 condition fail it. That single density is the number the locality arm has to beat.

main.equal_action_budget: Phase 2L Control 3, absolutely required. Movement, searching, defense, expansion and attack all consume the same instr_per_tick budget. No locality condition gives any entrant extra actions to compensate for movement; an out-of-reach attempt still costs its action. The cost of movement is part of the hypothesis.

gates.note: Predeclared before any main-stage result was inspected. Evaluated in the fixed order below; the gates are not weakened, reinterpreted, or supplemented after the fact.

go.G1: PRIMARY. Beta2 Sec 17 criterion 2 passes at >= 2 distinct density values among the six locality (L) conditions. The Ruleset-v2 control passes it at exactly one (S = 0.781) on the identical ladder.
go.G2: The locality arm scores 5/5 on the verbatim Sec 17 rubric at >= 4 of its 6 conditions, strictly more than the Ruleset-v2 control's 3 of 6 at the matched conditions.
go.G3: Expansion loses its residual edge without becoming useless: at the reference condition local_claimer's win rate is below the Ruleset-v2 control's claimer rate, AND the expansion role still wins >= 15% overall.
go.G4: Search is competitively relevant through its own mechanism: the search role wins >= 25% at >= 2 density values AND holds the highest capture-caused rate at those same conditions.
go.G5: No single archetype reaches >= 90% in two or more dissimilar rosters outside the declared negative control, at any locality condition.
go.G6: Context sensitivity survives: seat, layout and seed win-rate ranges are all non-zero at every locality condition, and the seed range at the reference condition is >= the Ruleset-v2 control's at a4096_b8.
go.G7: Pairwise-versus-group divergence is >= 10 pp at every locality condition.
go.G8: An observable movement/reconnaissance tradeoff exists: the mean MOVE share of actions is strictly between 0 and 0.5, and the highest-moving archetype exceeds the lowest-moving non-stationary archetype by >= 10 pp of action share.
go.G9: Bounded reach itself does the work: at the reference condition, >= 4 of the 33 roster/agent win rates in arm L have a Wilson interval disjoint from the same rate in the matched global-reach control arm G.
go.G10: Interaction stays frequent: mean encounter_ticks > 0 in >= 80% of rosters containing a dedicated search agent, at every locality condition.

modify.M1: Locality clearly improves one strategic axis but measurably damages another.
modify.M2: Only a very narrow R range survives the pilot (exactly one reach passes every rejection rule).
modify.M3: Movement is useful but the addressing semantics need revision (e.g. reach misses are unavoidable for a correctly written agent).
modify.M4: Core defense becomes too strong: a defense archetype wins >= 70% across >= 3 dissimilar rosters at the reference condition.
modify.M5: Locality works only after one clearly identified, small mechanic correction.

abandon.A1: Mean MOVE share of entrant actions >= 0.50 at the reference condition: agents spend most of their useful actions merely reaching one another.
abandon.A2: Criterion 2 passes at <= 1 density value in the locality arm (no wider than Ruleset v2) AND no other GO criterion is met.
abandon.A3: >= 50% of locality cells in search-containing rosters reach the tick limit with zero core captures.
abandon.A4: Expansion remains dominant for the same structural reason: local_claimer is the top-win archetype at >= 5 of the 6 locality conditions while the search role stays below 15% at all six.
abandon.A5: Search is strictly worse under locality than under the Ruleset-v2 control at every matched condition, on both win rate and capture-caused rate.
abandon.A6: One trivial policy dominates: local_camper leads >= 4 of the 11 rosters at the reference condition.
abandon.A7: Only near-global reach works: the pilot rejects every reach below arena_size/4, so no experimental condition is even available.
abandon.A8: Bounded reach contributed nothing: G9 fails, meaning arm L is statistically indistinguishable from the global-reach control arm G and any difference from Ruleset v2 is attributable to the ported agents rather than to locality.
abandon.A9: Context sensitivity is reduced: seat, layout and seed ranges are all lower at the reference condition than the Ruleset-v2 control's at a4096_b8.

decision_rule: 1. Evaluate every ABANDON criterion first. If any holds, the verdict is LOCALITY NOT VALIDATED -- ABANDON CURRENT V3 THESIS.
2. Otherwise, if G1 holds AND at least 6 of G1..G10 hold, the verdict is LOCALITY VALIDATED -- PROCEED TO MULTI-LOCUS RESEARCH.
3. Otherwise the verdict is LOCALITY PROMISING -- MODIFY BEFORE MULTI-LOCUS, and the MODIFY criteria that hold name the smallest locality-only follow-up.
4. INCONCLUSIVE / BLOCKED is reserved for a genuine methodological or architectural inability to decide, never used to avoid an ABANDON result.

python_only: Phase 2 locality research is Python-only. Ruleset v1 remains the historical VM/Redcode environment and is untouched; Ruleset v2 already established the Python-only gameplay precedent, and bytefray-rules-3-alpha1 declares supported_runtime_kinds = {python} for the same reason.
